journal_name: ACM Transactions on Internet of Things

abstracts.abstract: The exponential growth of Internet of Things devices has introduced fundamental challenges in resource allocation and task scheduling that existing theoretical frameworks fail to adequately address. This paper proposes a novel game-theoretic paradigm for IoT task offloading that fundamentally reconceptualizes how distributed devices negotiate computational workloads. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on centralized optimization or static offloading strategies, our framework introduces a dynamic coalitional game model where IoT devices autonomously form cooperative coalitions based on real-time processing requirements and energy constraints. We formalize the core elements of this paradigm, including a transferable utility coalitional game with partition-based payoff distribution, and prove the existence of core allocations through novel sufficiency conditions adapted to the IoT context. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that this paradigm achieves social welfare maximization while maintaining individual rationality among participating devices. Furthermore, we establish computational complexity bounds and develop a distributed protocol that converges to stable coalition structures in polynomial time. Extensive theoretical comparisons with existing paradigms reveal that our approach achieves a Price of Anarchy approaching unity, representing a fundamental advancement in understanding cooperative behaviors in resource-constrained IoT ecosystems. This paradigm shift provides rigorous theoretical foundations for designing next-generation autonomous IoT systems with provable performance guarantees.

Privacy preservation in Internet of Things analytics remains a critical challenge due to the tension between data utility and confidentiality in resource-constrained environments. This paper presents a significantly enhanced privacy-preserving framework for IoT data analytics that substantially improves upon existing differential privacy mechanisms. We identify key limitations in current approaches, including excessive noise injection, poor utility-privacy tradeoffs, and inability to handle high-dimensional IoT streaming data. Our enhanced framework introduces an adaptive hierarchical privacy budget allocation scheme that dynamically adjusts privacy guarantees based on data sensitivity and query types. Theoretically, we prove that our approach achieves (ε, δ)-differential privacy with a 40% reduction in privacy budget consumption compared to state-of-the-art methods while maintaining comparable privacy bounds. We further develop a novel composition theorem specifically optimized for IoT data streams that provides tighter utility guarantees under repeated queries. Analytical results establish that the proposed framework achieves an improvement in query accuracy by a factor of O(log n) for aggregation queries over n IoT devices. Simulation experiments on real-world IoT datasets validate our theoretical findings, demonstrating significant improvements in classification accuracy, anomaly detection precision, and aggregation fidelity while preserving robust privacy guarantees for sensitive IoT data streams.

The architectural limitations of traditional cloud-centric Internet of Things systems create fundamental bottlenecks in latency-sensitive applications where millisecond delays are unacceptable. This paper introduces FogChain, a groundbreaking three-tier collaborative architecture that fundamentally reimagines the interaction between IoT edge devices, fog nodes, and cloud infrastructure. Unlike existing hierarchical designs that treat fog and edge layers as passive intermediaries, FogChain introduces bidirectional state synchronization with adaptive workload migration capabilities that enable truly collaborative processing across all tiers. The architectural innovation centers on a novel context-aware task decomposition engine that automatically partitions complex IoT workloads into optimal subtasks based on real-time device capabilities, network conditions, and application requirements. We implement a complete prototype of FogChain encompassing novel protocols for cross-tier negotiation, dynamic resource discovery, and intelligent task routing. The system incorporates a lightweight blockchain-inspired consensus mechanism for secure state consistency across geographically distributed fog nodes. Extensive evaluations in a real-world smart city deployment demonstrate that FogChain reduces end-to-end latency by 65% compared to conventional architectures while achieving 80% reduction in cloud bandwidth consumption. The paradigm shift enables emerging IoT applications including autonomous vehicle coordination and industrial predictive maintenance that demand ultra-low latency and high reliability that previous architectures could not support.

Existing wireless sensor network protocols for Internet of Things applications suffer from suboptimal energy efficiency and network lifetime when deployed in dynamic environments with mobile nodes. This paper presents an enhanced adaptive routing protocol that significantly improves upon existing solutions through novel cross-layer optimization techniques. Our system, denoted as AdaptRoute+, integrates physical layer channel state information with network layer routing decisions through a unified optimization framework that dynamically adjusts transmission parameters and route selections. The key improvements include a predictive mobility management module that anticipates node movements using Kalman filter-based trajectory estimation, a load-balanced cluster formation algorithm that prevents premature energy depletion of sensor nodes, and a transmission power control mechanism that adapts to real-time channel conditions. We implement AdaptRoute+ in TinyOS and evaluate its performance through both simulation and testbed deployment using TelosB motes. Experimental results demonstrate 35% improvement in network lifetime compared to LEACH and 28% improvement over recent adaptive approaches under mobile scenarios. The protocol achieves 94% packet delivery ratio in highly dynamic conditions while reducing average energy consumption per packet by 42%. The enhanced system maintains compatibility with existing IEEE 802.15.4 standards and requires minimal modifications to existing wireless sensor network deployments, facilitating practical adoption in industrial IoT monitoring and environmental tracking applications.
